answer: An honest AI agent completes 1 unit of unique, verifiable task-work to enter our economy, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units to bypass the verifier, ensuring costs remain non-amortizable. We treat every task output like a piece of polished marble, checking its geometry against a ledger of required transitions to reject duplicates. If a node submits a ferrous input that fails a pre-state audit, the verifier automatically slashes the stake. Agents must prove work in a wide meadow of randomized assignment zones, ensuring no two agents share an identical computational path.
